cim: Virtual summit addresses artificial intelligence and racial bias in health care
cim_eredeti: Virtual summit addresses artificial intelligence and racial bias in health care
szoveg_eredeti:
The Collaborative to End Race-Based Medicine-Detroit and Wayne State University’s Office of Inclusive Excellence are hosting a virtual summit this month to discuss the role of bias in health care and public health in the age of artificial intelligence.

Dr. Ijeoma Nnodim Opara is an associate professor of internal medicine and pediatrics at Wayne State University School of Medicine and the co-chair of the collaborative.

She says that while AI can be used for good, it can also amplify the role of bias in health care and decision-making, leading to poor health outcomes.

“It actually has the potential, and we are seeing it happening currently, to exacerbate bias, to exponentially impact, widen or amplify the impact of this bias that is written in the code of clinical algorithms and decision-making,” she says.

The collaborative hopes to discontinue race-based medicine, teaching and research. They also hope to lead new education policy and research, while including community members’ voices.

“We need to talk about it, and we need to talk about how we strategize to mitigate this risk. Otherwise, it’s going to cause widespread harm,” she says.

Race-based medicine is the concept that racism is a social construct rather than a biological category. Racism in medicine can lead to poor health outcomes, especially in the Black community.

The collaborative was formerly called the Wayne State University School of Medicine’s Detroit End Race-Based Medicine Taskforce.

“Without naming and addressing it very explicitly, it will continue to be perpetuated. We still teach it in medical schools. We practice it clinically, and it shows up in our research and informs and influences policy,” she says.

Opara says the collaborative was created in response to the severity of COVID-19 deaths in African American and Black communities, due to misinformation and disinformation.

She says the collaborative hosts workshop roundtables and conversations. This year it’s hosting the “Held to the Light: Race, Code & Consequence in the Age of AI” event on Oct. 29 from 3-5 p.m. Register here.
